title: feat(studio): preview record pages against a real sample record
body:
## What

The Studio page editor's **Preview** tab rendered a `type: 'record'` page's `record:*` blocks (details / highlights / path / alert / quick_actions) as the **"bind a record to preview"** placeholder. The metadata editor has no record route, so the author was designing blind — list and home/app page previews already showed live data, but record pages did not.

## How

The preview now mirrors the runtime `RecordDetailView`:

- Fetches a handful of real records of the bound `object` (`$top=50`), with **lookup / master_detail fields `$expand`ed** (via `buildExpandFields`) so they render display names (e.g. *Website Relaunch*) instead of raw foreign-key IDs.
- **Auto-binds the first record** and wraps the canvas in `<RecordContextProvider>`.
- Adds a **"Preview record" dropdown** so the author can switch records; `visible` CEL expressions and per-record field values re-render live.

No-op for non-record pages and for record objects with no rows (the existing placeholder still shows).

## Verification

Against the `app-showcase` backend, previewing `showcase_task_detail` (record page bound to `showcase_task`):

- `record:path` / `record:highlights` / `record:details` / `record:quick_actions` populate with real field values.
- The `project` lookup expands to its name rather than a raw id.
- The `record:alert` banner (`visible: "record.status == 'in_review'"`) **hides** for `done`/`backlog` records and **appears** when the picked record is `in_review` — confirming CEL evaluates against the chosen record.
- `pnpm vitest run PagePreview.test.tsx` → 3/3 pass; `tsc --noEmit` on `@object-ui/app-shell` → 0 errors.

Scoped to the record-page preview only (`PagePreview.tsx` + its test + a changeset).
